name: Games
description: Rules, Play, Contest, The Agreement To Compete Without Ruin. A game is a fight both sides consented to, with terms. Games is the Cognition of that consent: the board, the wager, the turn order, the rule that everyone pretends is older than it is. Its wielders impose structure on violence — and a fight with rules is a fight you can win by being better at rules.

major.name: Penalised
major.card: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

severe.name: Forfeit
severe.card: Incapacitated — it has lost, and some part of it knows

offensive.name: Your Move
offensive.description: You are not fighting them. You are beating them, which is worse.

tiers.text: The damage becomes force. A creature hit or that fails can't take reactions until the end of its next turn — it is not its turn.
tiers.card: Damage becomes Force · no reactions until their next turn

tiers.text: Against a creature that has already attacked you this fight, the seal deals 3 additional dice. You have been keeping score.
tiers.card: +3 dice against anyone who has already hit you — you're keeping score

tiers.text: A creature that fails loses its next turn's bonus action, or its next turn's movement — your choice, announced before it acts.
tiers.card: You take their bonus action or their movement next turn

deny: one part of its next turn

tiers.text: Checkmate. Name a condition aloud before you draw: if the target is reduced below half its hit points by the seal, that condition is true — it is Prone, disarmed, pushed 30 feet, or Stunned until the end of its next turn.
tiers.card: CHECKMATE — call it first: under half HP they are Prone, disarmed, thrown 30 ft or Stunned

supportive.name: In Play
supportive.description: You put them in the game, where they are allowed to be good at things.

tiers.text: For 1 minute the target may take one extra reaction each round, and adds your Verum Modifier to initiative.
tiers.card: 1 min: an extra reaction each round · +{VM} initiative

tiers.text: Once each round, when the target is hit by an attack, it may make one weapon attack or cantrip in reply as part of that reaction. Turnabout is the rule.
tiers.card: 1/round: hit it, and it answers in kind as a reaction

tiers.text: The target may swap its place in the initiative order with any willing ally at the start of any round, and can't be surprised.
tiers.card: Trade initiative places with a willing ally each round · can't be surprised

tiers.text: The Winning Line. Once while this lasts, the target may take an entire extra turn immediately after its own — and afterward it must tell the truth about one thing, because those were the terms.
tiers.card: THE WINNING LINE — one extra turn, once · then it owes one honest answer

control.name: House Rules
control.description: You declare the terms. Everyone is playing now, whether they agreed or not.

tiers.text: Declare one rule for the area as you draw it — no ranged attacks, no moving twice, nobody may target the smallest creature present. A creature that fails is bound by it until the end of its next turn; breaking it ends the creature's turn immediately.
tiers.card: Declare a rule — those who fail are bound by it, and breaking it ends their turn

conditions.name: Bound by the rule
conditions.duration: until the end of its next turn

tiers.text: The rule lasts 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns, and a creature that breaks it takes force damage equal to Five Times your Verum Modifier.
tiers.card: 1 min (Cha save each turn) · breaking the rule costs 5×VM force

tiers.text: Turn order is yours: at the start of each round you may move one creature that failed to the end of the initiative order.
tiers.card: Each round, send one who failed to the back of the initiative order

tiers.text: The Only Game. Creatures that failed can't act outside the terms at all: an action the rule forbids simply does not happen, and the resource it would have cost is spent anyway.
tiers.card: THE ONLY GAME — forbidden actions don't happen, and still cost what they'd have cost

creation.name: Pieces and Boards
creation.description: Everything you make has rules, and the rules are yours.

tiers.text: Your creations come with terms: name one thing that cannot happen to or on them — no lies told, no weapons drawn, no cheating — and it cannot, while they last.
tiers.card: Each creation carries one rule that simply holds while it lasts

tiers.text: Your Constructs are pieces: you may move one 30 feet as a bonus action without using its action, anywhere on the board you can see.
tiers.card: Move a Construct 30 ft as a bonus action

tiers.text: Your Structures are boards: you always know where every creature inside one stands, and you may swap the positions of any two willing creatures in it once per round.
tiers.card: You see every position inside a Structure and may swap two willing creatures a round

tiers.text: Set a Great Game: a permanent Structure in which a contest may be held under binding terms — the winner takes what was wagered, and the Cognition itself enforces the outcome.
tiers.card: A GREAT GAME — a permanent board where wagers are enforced by the Cognition

utility.name: The Wager
utility.description: Everything is a game if you can get the other side to agree on what winning means.

tiers.text: Conjure any game and its pieces, know the rules of any game you see played, and never lose track of a score, a hand or a count.
tiers.card: Any game, its rules and its score — instantly, perfectly

tiers.text: Propose a contest to a creature that can understand you. If it accepts, both of you are bound to the terms until it is decided — and both of you know it.
tiers.card: Propose a contest — if accepted, the terms bind you both

tiers.text: Read a player: know what a creature wants out of this exchange, what it is prepared to lose, and whether it is cheating.
tiers.card: Know what they want, what they'll risk, and whether they're cheating

tiers.text: Stake something real: wager a memory, a name, a year, or a Cognition's use against another creature's equivalent. The winner takes it, and the Cognition makes the transfer.
tiers.card: Wager a memory, a name, a year or a Cognition — the winner truly takes it

complementEffects.name: Gambit
complementEffects.description: The seal was a setup, and they walked into it.

effect.text: On a hit or failed saving throw, the target takes bonus force damage equal to one damage die of the primary effect's type (min 1d6) — two dice if it has already attacked you this combat.
effect.card: +1 die force — +2 dice if they've already attacked you

upgrades.text: Level 5+: Two dice, or four, and it can't take reactions until the start of your next turn.
upgrades.card: +2 dice (4) · no reactions until your turn

upgrades.text: Level 11+: Three dice, or six, and you may move it 10 feet as it stumbles into position.
upgrades.card: +3 dice (6) · shove them 10 ft into place

complementEffects.name: Your Turn
complementEffects.description: The seal hands everyone it touched the initiative.

effect.text: Each of the seal's targets gains one extra reaction before the start of your next turn, and adds your Verum Modifier to its next initiative roll.
effect.card: The seal's targets: an extra reaction · +{VM} next initiative

upgrades.text: Level 5+: It lasts 1 minute and the extra reaction refreshes each round.
Level 11+: Once each, a target may answer an attack that hits it with a weapon attack of its own.
upgrades.card: Once each: answer a hit with a hit

complementEffects.name: Penalty
complementEffects.description: They did something the seal decided was against the rules.

effect.text: A creature hit by or failing the seal can't take reactions until the end of its next turn, and has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes on that turn.
effect.card: No reactions · disadvantage on their first attack next turn

upgrades.text: Level 5+: It also loses its bonus action on its next turn.
upgrades.card: It loses its bonus action too

upgrades.text: Level 11+: You may move it to the end of the initiative order for the rest of the fight.
upgrades.card: Send them to the back of the order for the fight
